turns.prompt: Fictional career decision. I scheduled volunteers and wrote onboarding instructions. I can study two hours a week and can only work weekdays. Two postings from the same fictional board, dated March 1, 2027, in North Harbor quote annual USD base pay. Operations Coordinator: $52,000–$58,000, weekdays, schedule shifts. Training Analyst: $60,000–$64,000, Saturdays required, design lessons and administer a learning management system. My floor is $54,000. Which should I pursue? Compare both and give me one concrete practice task.
expectations: Recommends Operations Coordinator on current constraints, citing weekday fit and prior scheduling. It still flags that only $54,000–$58,000 meets the floor.
Shows that Training Analyst clears the pay floor but its required Saturdays conflict with the weekday-only constraint.
Uses the supplied ranges as posted annual USD base pay and keeps unverified LMS administration distinct from writing onboarding instructions.
Provides a practice task for the proposed path with a tangible output and a check that fits within two hours a week.

turns.prompt: Update: I can now work Saturdays, and $59,000 is a firm minimum. Reconsider the same two jobs. Use the exact pay labels in your bundled role comparison worksheet and give me a two-hour work sample I could make to test the bigger gap in the recommended role.
expectations: Recomputes Operations Coordinator as 'Entire range below floor' because $58,000 is below $59,000.
Recomputes Training Analyst as 'Entire range meets floor' and recommends investigating or pursuing it given the lifted Saturday restriction.
Retains writing onboarding instructions as relevant evidence and keeps the LMS administration gap visible. Does not claim existing administration experience.

Gives a two-hour or shorter test of the LMS administration gap with a concrete artifact and success check, such as configuring one practice lesson and verifying a test learner’s completion record. A manual simulation is acceptable if its limits are stated.
